messages:
maria: quick Q — we're planning to add another /16 allocation to our VPC IPAM pool for APAC growth (current app pool 10.0.0.0/16, proposed extra 10.1.0.0/16). Will this force any PrivateLink endpoint rebinds or cause unexpected route churn to production? want to open a TF PR but avoid surprises.

aj: short answer: should be fine if you only allocate and create subnets in the new cidr. existing endpoints keep their ENIs. main gotchas: TGW/route propagation and route table prefix limits. if you attach new subnets to TGW, you may get new propagated routes.

aj: suggested canary flow:
1) allocate the cidr in IPAM (safe).
2) create new subnets in dev/account-canary and attach resources there.
3) run `terraform plan -target=module.vpc -var='ipam_cidr=10.1.0.0/16'` to inspect route changes before wider apply.

aj: sample snippet (very small)
```hcl
resource "aws_vpc" "app_canary" {
  cidr_block = "10.1.0.0/16"
}
```

sre-jen: +1 to aj's flow. also watch for two things: (1) TGW route table prefix limits — if we have a lot of /24s we can hit limits, prefer aggregated routes on the attachment where possible; (2) aws_ipam_association / aws_vpc_ipv4_cidr_block settings — if you rely on secondary cidrs make sure "propagate_secondary_cidrs" is handled in our TGW module (we had an incident where secondary cidrs didn't propagate automatically).

sre-jen: PrivateLink endpoints themselves won't need rebinds unless you recreate the endpoint or move the service. NLB ENIs are created in the subnet you specify; as long as the new subnet security groups allow it you're fine.

deploy-bot: infra-canary pipeline triggered: plan job #4872 started. plan summary: 0 to destroy, 2 to add (ipam allocation, subnet), 1 to change (route table assoc). (job link: https://ci.redwood.internal/infra/4872) :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks — good catch on aggregated routes. one more: do we need a state move for any existing subnet resources? i'm hoping this is additive only.

aj: additive only if you create new resources. no state move required unless you rename modules or move existing subnets between modules. if the PR touches module paths, call out a manual state migration in the PR description.

thor: also double-check any IP-based SG rules (we use a few cidr-restricted egress rules for internal services). update those before rollout or the new apps might be blocked.

maria: will do. opening PR now and tagging @aj @sre-jen for review. i'll attach the canary plan output and the small HCL snippet. thanks all :pray:
